problem:
Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P02.1, P02.2, P02.3, P02.4. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
1     Regularization of arbitrary classical psh functions
Active items: P02.1, P02.2, P02.3, P02.4. Status: Open in the residual scope.

1.1   Atomic targets
P02.1 (T3): Decreasing semipositive real-PL regularization
Characterize the higher-dimensional good strict analytic spaces on which every classically psh
function is, near every point, the pointwise decreasing limit of semipositive real PL functions.
The starting function is arbitrary in the classical curve-test class; invariant continuous toric
functions form only a known special case.

P02.2 (T3): Decreasing locally Fubini–Study regularization
For the same arbitrary classical psh starting class, characterize the spaces admitting local
decreasing approximations by locally Fubini–Study functions. This asks for the Fubini–Study
conclusion itself, rather than merely real-PL or smooth approximation.

P02.3 (T3): Decreasing weakly smooth psh regularization
Characterize the higher-dimensional good strict spaces on which every classically psh function
has local decreasing weakly smooth psh approximants. Weak smoothness is deﬁned through
harmonic tropicalizations and must not be identiﬁed with ordinary CLD smoothness.

P02.4 (T4): Decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth psh regularization
Characterize the spaces on which every classical psh function has local decreasing approxima-
tions by ordinary CLD-smooth psh functions. The ordinary smooth requirement is part of
the target; a weakly smooth sequence alone does not solve it.

1.2   What constitutes a solution
Give precise geometric hypotheses for the requested local approximation, a construction in
the speciﬁed approximant class and a proof of decreasing convergence, or counterexamples
that establish the sharp failure range. Treat scalar extension and overlaps explicitly; a net
must not be silently replaced by a sequence.

1.3   Full statement and detailed state of the art
Problem 1.1. On which higher-dimensional good strict analytic spaces is every classically
psh function locally a decreasing limit of semipositive real PL, locally Fubini–Study, weakly
smooth psh, or CLD-smooth psh functions?

    The four targets must be separated. Real PL functions on the relative interior satisfy
the three-way comparison of Book Theorem 69.8.1. On smooth boundaryless curves, [GJR26,
Proposition 15.11] gives decreasing weakly smooth regularization locally on each relatively
compact open subset. Wanner’s published CLD-smooth regularization had the additional
residue-ﬁeld or curve hypotheses stated in [Wan19, Corollary 5.4]; Book Theorem 19.3.4 re-
moves them for continuous current-psh functions on smooth proper algebraic curves. Weakly
smooth harmonic functions need not be CLD-smooth.
    The attempted higher-dimensional proof combines local formal models, regularized max-
ima, and harmonic tropicalizations. Curvewise approximation does not by itself glue: the
approximants must be compatible on overlapping tropical charts and after scalar extension.

                                               7

Nor may a nonmetrizable net be replaced by a sequence without a countable extraction argu-
ment. The general problem is open; the curve and PL cases are veriﬁed boundary cases.
    There is a strictly invariant higher-dimensional semipositive-real-PL endpoint as well. On
an ordinary open convex chamber of a split torus, a ﬁnite continuous maximal-compact-torus-
invariant psh function descends to a ﬁnite convex tropical potential. On every displayed
good strictly analytic inverse image of a nonempty ordinary open set compactly contained
in the chamber, ﬁnite tangent-plane approximations of gently shifted radial smoothings give
one decreasing semipositive real-PL sequence. The explicit pullbacks are CLD-psh, hence
classically psh, and the real-PL comparison then gives semipositivity without separatedness,
boundarylessness, or pure-dimensionality. This begins with the invariant current-psh class, not
every classically psh function. Its real-PL conclusion by itself does not identify the sequence
as locally Fubini–Study or weakly smooth; the two separate companion arguments below add
those regularities.
Corollary 1.1 (Invariant toric decreasing semipositive real-PL regularization). Let K be
a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean ﬁeld, let T = Gnm,K be a split torus with
maximal compact torus S, and let O ⊂ NR ≃ Rn be a nonempty ordinary open convex set.
Put V = trop−1 (O). Let B be a nonempty ordinary open set with B ⋐ O, and assume
that W := trop−1 (B) is good and strictly K-analytic. If u : V → R is a ﬁnite continuous
S-invariant psh function in the CLD-current sense, there is a sequence of ﬁnite S-invariant
semipositive real-PL functions
                                      vj : W −→ R
that decreases pointwise and locally uniformly to u|W .
   There is also a strictly invariant higher-dimensional locally Fubini–Study endpoint. Rather
than regularizing each real-PL approximant on a potentially changing neighbourhood, ﬁnite
supporting planes are rounded directly to the character lattice on one ﬁxed relatively compact
tropical open set. Their maxima are locally Fubini–Study and retain a quantitative interstage
gap, so they form one decreasing sequence on that open set.
Corollary 1.2 (Invariant toric decreasing locally Fubini–Study regularization). Let K be
a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean ﬁeld, let T = Gnm,K be a split torus with
maximal compact torus S, and let O ⊂ NR ≃ Rn be a nonempty ordinary open convex set.
Put V = trop−1 (O). If u : V → R is a ﬁnite continuous S-invariant psh function, then, for
every nonempty ordinary open set B with B ⋐ O, there is a sequence of ﬁnite S-invariant
locally Fubini–Study functions
                                   vj : trop−1 (B) −→ R
that decreases pointwise and locally uniformly to u|trop−1 (B) . Thus this class belongs locally to
the ﬁrst decreasing locally Fubini–Study stage.
    There is also a strictly invariant higher-dimensional CLD-smooth endpoint. On one open
convex chamber of a split torus, the ﬁnite continuous maximal-compact-torus-invariant psh
functions pull back from ﬁnite convex tropical potentials. Radial molliﬁcation on the tropical
chamber therefore gives a decreasing sequence of ordinary CLD-smooth psh functions after
pullback. This is a current-psh invariant subfamily, not a result for all classically psh functions.
Corollary 1.3 (Invariant toric decreasing CLD-smooth regularization). Let K be a complete
nontrivially valued non-Archimedean ﬁeld, let T = Gnm,K be a split torus with maximal compact
torus S, and let O ⊂ NR ≃ Rn be a nonempty ordinary open convex set. Put V = trop−1 (O).
If u : V → R is a ﬁnite continuous S-invariant psh function, then, for every nonempty
ordinary open set B with B ⋐ O, there is a sequence of ﬁnite S-invariant CLD-smooth psh
functions
                                   uj : trop−1 (B) −→ R

                                                 8

that decreases pointwise and locally uniformly to u|trop−1 (B) . Thus u belongs locally to the ﬁrst
decreasing CLD-smooth psh stage.

    The same invariant-toric sequence also has the weakly smooth regularity required by the
third target. This uses only the inclusion of ordinary CLD-smooth forms into weakly smooth
forms and retains the same CLD-current positivity; it is not a comparison of two positivity
notions.

Corollary 1.4 (Invariant toric decreasing weakly smooth regularization). Under the hypothe-
ses of Corollary 1.3, the sequence (uj )j there is a decreasing sequence of ﬁnite S-invariant
weakly smooth psh functions on trop−1 (B), converging pointwise and locally uniformly to
u|trop−1 (B) . Consequently, this ﬁnite continuous invariant current-psh class belongs locally to
the ﬁrst decreasing weakly smooth psh stage.

    The convexity imposed above is only a device for making one common regularization neigh-
bourhood; it is not a germwise restriction on the toric domain. Indeed, the four conclusions
localize simultaneously on an arbitrary tropical open set.

Corollary 1.5 (Invariant toric germwise regularization on arbitrary tropical domains). Let
K be a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean ﬁeld, let T = Gnm,K be a split torus with
maximal compact torus S, let Ω ⊂ NR ≃ Rn be an ordinary open set, and put U = trop−1 (Ω).
If u : U → R is ﬁnite, continuous, S-invariant, and psh in the CLD-current sense, then every
x ∈ Ω has ordinary open convex neighbourhoods

                                         x∈B⋐O⋐Ω

for which u|trop−1 (B) is a pointwise and locally uniform decreasing limit, respectively, of ﬁnite
S-invariant locally Fubini–Study functions, weakly smooth psh functions, and CLD-smooth
psh functions. If in addition trop−1 (B) is good and strictly K-analytic, it is also such a limit
of ﬁnite S-invariant semipositive real-PL functions. Thus all four displayed invariant-toric
endpoint conclusions hold germwise on every tropical open domain.
